title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed first-year examination paper: Université des Sciences et Techniques du Languedoc (Montpellier), DEUG A 1ère année, Maths Appliquées, June 1981 session, 'Epreuve d'Analyse', 3 hours. Grothendieck was teaching at Montpellier then, so it was probably kept with the notes or used as scrap paper (the verso may have carried notes). The handwritten '184' is an archival folio number. It has no connection to the previous page, which is a dimension count for stable curves (μ(Σ) = μ(g,ν) − μ, with μ the number of double points).

Part I.1. The equation is x y y' + 2y² = 1/(x³(x+1)²). Put z = y². The equation becomes x z' + 4z = 2/(x³(x+1)²), that is (x⁴z)' = 2/(x+1)². Integrating gives x⁴z = C − 2/(x+1). The condition y(2) = 1/(4√3) gives z(2) = 1/48, so 16/48 = C − 2/3 and C = 1. Hence x⁴z = (x−1)/(x+1), and taking the positive root, y = (1/x²)√((x−1)/(x+1)) on ]1,+∞[. This solution is exactly the integrand of part 2.

Part I.2. Put x = 1/u. Then F(A) = ∫_{1/A}^{1} √((1−u)/(1+u)) du = ∫ (1−u)/√(1−u²) du = [arcsin u + √(1−u²)]_{1/A}^{1}. So F(A) = π/2 − arcsin(1/A) − √(1 − 1/A²).

Part I.3. As A → +∞, F(A) → π/2 − 1.

Part II. The curve is x = t(3t²−2)/(1−t²), y = t⁴/(1−t²).
- Symmetry: x(−t) = −x(t) and y(−t) = y(t), so the curve is symmetric about the y-axis and t ≥ 0 suffices.
- Derivatives: dx/dt = −(3t²−1)(t²−2)/(1−t²)² and dy/dt = 2t³(2−t²)/(1−t²)². Both vanish at t = √2, which is a cusp at the point (−4√2, −4). dx/dt also vanishes at t = 1/√3.
- Near the origin: x ~ −2t and y ~ t⁴, so the tangent is horizontal with very flat contact.
- t → 1: y/x → 1 and y − x = −t(t²−2t−2)/(1+t) → 3/2, so the oblique asymptote is y = x + 3/2.
- t → ∞: x = −3t + t/(1−t²) and y = −t² − 1 + 1/(1−t²). The asymptotic parabola is X = −3t, Y = −t² − 1, that is Y = −X²/9 − 1.

ideas.what: Routine undergraduate exercises: a Bernoulli-type ODE reduced to a linear one via z = y², an elementary integral by the substitution x = 1/u, and a parametric curve study (symmetry, cusp, asymptotes, asymptotic parabola)
ideas.where_published: not applicable (department exam paper, likely not authored by Grothendieck)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed first-year analysis exam from Montpellier (June 1981), filed among the Teichmüller notes, with no research content. Its only interest is historical: it documents Grothendieck's teaching environment at the time.
transcription_corrections: The right-hand side of the ODE is 1/(x³(x+1)²). The faint 'x' is confirmed by the computation, since the solution y = x⁻²√((x−1)/(x+1)) matches the integrand of part 2.
Part II.2 should read 'en fonction de t' (the 'de t.' wraps onto the next line in the original).
'184' is the archival folio number handwritten at the bottom left, not part of the exam.
